title: 7/12 eve-of-break restart loop: ~47 duplicate CRITICAL health DMs, blind restart_spike, confounded predicted_vs_realized CRITICAL
tier_reason: liveness failure (Restart=always crash-loop for ~39 min) with an alert storm (~47 identical CRITICAL DMs)

contract.text: After the last game of a slate the scheduler idles until the next day's wake; a completed day is not re-walked, a health incident produces at most one DM per identity per day, and the restart detector sees restart storms.
contract.source: docs/audit/2026-07-12-eve-of-break-restart-loop.md; scheduler step 7 / _next_day_wakeup (audit E1); health DM dispatcher design (once per day)

mechanism.text: run_day step 7 called compute_wakeup_time(fetch_schedule(tomorrow)) directly; for an empty tomorrow (All-Star break) it returned TODAY 10:00, already 8.6 h past
_idle_until_next_wakeup silently returned on a past wakeup, so run_day exited cleanly and Restart=always relaunched it every ~48 s; each relaunch re-walked the completed day
dispatch_dm_for_health_alerts, designed to run once per day, sent unconditionally on every re-walk: ~47 identical CRITICAL DMs
restart_spike advanced its checkpoint every run, so 48 s re-walks moved the baseline +1 at a time and the storm never summed past its +3 threshold
predicted_vs_realized compared the primary's p against the DAY-level result (a DD day needs both legs), which mechanically inflated the gap into a CRITICAL

mitigated.action: operator session stopped bts-scheduler (left down pending the fix)

verified_recovered.how: deploy canary: scheduler + dashboard active, dashboard HTTP 2xx

residual.text: _idle_until_next_wakeup still returns on a past wakeup (now logged loudly) rather than substituting a guessed wake, so any other past-wakeup path would again end run_day into Restart=always.
dd_pair_realized_shortfall stayed quiet during the DD-leg slump (its drift-vs-baseline design dilutes a slump spanning two windows); not changed in this batch.
drift_critical was raised 0.12 -> 0.25 pending a day-block bootstrap recalibration (queued).

watchdog.trigger: bts-scheduler NRestarts rises by 3 or more within 20 minutes, or the same health incident identity is DMed more than once in a day
watchdog.recovery_assertion: after the fix, NRestarts is stable for 30+ minutes, the scheduler logs a next wake dated tomorrow or later, and the dashboard answers

evidence.what: clean EOD exit at 18:36:16 ET; Restart=always relaunched every ~48 s, each relaunch re-walked the completed day and sent a new CRITICAL DM; NRestarts 3 -> 50 (~47 DMs) until the operator stopped the unit at 19:15 ET

evidence.locator: same memo §Monitoring verdicts during the loop
evidence.what: the external check_heartbeat cron caught the churn in 4 minutes (NRestarts +5 within 20 min) and cut the healthchecks.io ping; restart_spike was blinded by its own checkpoint
step 7's raw compute_wakeup_time returned today 10:00 for the empty tomorrow; the idle no-op returned; the time-only wake log hid the wrong day
47 identical CRITICAL DMs from the unconditional dispatcher; restart_spike aliasing

evidence.locator: commit 230f65c message body; memo §Why the CRITICAL fired at all
evidence.what: the CRITICAL compared the primary's p with the day-level result on DD days; per-slot grading re-scores it as a WARN
